# Planning

## How To Build

A Planning should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A Planning should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, integration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [Theme](../../ui/theme/index.md#theme): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Pitch

A plain, quick list of the work still to do, as Linear keeps issues: stories written ahead of time, each saying how it will be sent, Code, Chain, Spec, Ask, or Freeform, gathered into the next sprint and sent to the agent in order, all at once.

## Description

Planning opens in a tab of its own in the body, "Planning", with a checklist icon, as a file opens, as the [Body](../application/Body.md#body) says, from the ribbon's Planning tab or the palette's "Planning". It is a kanban board, filling the body beneath the tab bar, as the [Body](../application/Body.md#body) places it, from the tab bar down to the bottom of the body and from the body's left edge to its right, since the chat input isn't shown while Planning's tab is selected. Its sections sit side by side as columns, in the order work moves, left to right: "Draft", the first, "Backlog", "Next sprint", "Current sprint", and "Done", then "Findings", the last, as research says. Draft holds rough stories, ideas written down quickly that aren't ready to plan yet, until they are moved to the Backlog. The Draft column is not drafting: "Draft stories", the Backlog's button that asks the agent for proposals, as creating says, is apart from it and never puts anything in it. Each column is headed by its name and count, with its actions, as the layout says, and holds its stories as cards, one beneath another. Every column is always there, whatever it holds; one with nothing in it shows its empty state, as the states say.

## Stories

A story is one piece of work, written as it will be sent: a title, a prompt, and how it will be sent. Each is a story card in its column, as the parts say, quiet and dense, as Linear keeps an issue, showing all a story shows: a drag grip at its top left; its title beside it, the card's one primary thing, in the body's text colour, wrapping onto a second line and cut off with an ellipsis only after that; and beneath the title, a single muted property row of small

### Items

a small mode picker, a pill reading its mode, "Code", "Chain",

"Spec", "Ask", or "Freeform", in that mode's colour, as the [PromptModes](../prompt-mode/modes/index.md#prompt-modes) colours it; its step count and a small icon for anything attached, when it has them; and, once it has been sent, its status, as a task's is shown, at the row's right. Hovering a card shows a menu button at its top right. A story has no Send of its own, as the sprint says.
A column is too narrow to open a story in place, so clicking a card never expands it beneath itself or moves the cards below it: it opens the story in the side panel, docked at the board's right, as the layout places it and the parts draw a panel, headed by the story's title. The panel holds all an open story holds: its title, editable in place; its prompt, in a [GrowingTextInput](../../ui/components/growing-text-input/index.md#growing-text-input) with the chat input's highlighting, completions, and slicing, as the [ChatInput](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input) has, and its attachments beneath; its parameters, its mode, model, effort, and Slice, as the chat input shows them; its steps, with Add step, as its steps say; and its Spec citations, as the spec grounding says. Every change is saved as it is made. While its story is open, its card stays highlighted, its line in the theme's accent, so which story the panel shows is always plain. Only one story is open at a time: clicking another card opens that one in the panel instead. Escape, the panel's close button, or clicking the open story's card again closes it, and its card's highlight with it.

## Creating

Creating a story is quick, as adding a card is in Trello and adding an issue is in Linear: a story is added in the list it belongs in, right where it will sit. Draft, the Backlog, and Next sprint each end with an "Add story" line at their foot, beneath their last card, or beneath their empty state when they have none. Clicking it opens a composer in its place: a blank story card, drawn as the parts draw one, whose title is a text box, focused, in the mode last picked for a story, with nothing else to fill in. Typing a title and pressing Enter adds the story to that list, where the composer was, and opens another composer beneath it, so a list can be written down without the mouse. Enter with the title empty adds nothing. Escape discards the composer, and whatever was typed in it, and the "Add story" line comes back; clicking away while its title is empty discards it too, and clicking away with a title typed adds the story, as Enter does, but opens no other composer. A story added this way is not opened in the side panel; its card is there to be clicked, as the stories say, once more than its title is wanted.
Hovering Draft's, the Backlog's, or Next sprint's heading shows a labelled "+ Add" button in it, as the layout places it, which opens the composer at the top of that list, above its first card, so a story can go first without being dragged there; Enter adds it there and opens the next composer beneath it, so stories written one after another keep the order they were written in. Ctrl+N (Cmd+N on macOS) while Planning has focus opens the composer at the foot of the list that has focus, Draft, the Backlog, or Next sprint, as the keyboard says, and at the foot of Next sprint when none of them has it. Only one composer is open at a time: opening another discards an empty one and adds one with a title, as clicking away does. Current sprint, Done, and Findings have no "Add story" line, no "+ Add", and no composer, and Ctrl+N never adds a story to them.
A story goes into the list it was added to, then: Draft, the Backlog, or Next sprint, whichever composer it was written in. A duplicate goes into its original's list, just beneath it, and a story added from an Ask answer's card with "Add to sprint" goes into Next sprint, at its end. An accepted proposal for a new story, from drafting, research, or an Ask answer's proposal card, still goes into the Backlog, at its end, as the proposal cards say, and reaches a sprint only once it is moved to Next sprint; nothing the agent proposes ever goes into Draft. A story can always be moved among Draft, the Backlog, and Next sprint afterwards, as the sprint says. Adding a story never starts a sprint by itself, except where Start automatically starts one when a story is added to an empty Next sprint, as auto start says; a story added to Draft or the Backlog never starts one. A title with no prompt sends its title as its prompt.
A story can also be prompted into existence: "Draft stories", a button beside the Backlog's heading, and Draft Stories on the [RibbonPlanningTab](../../ui/components/ribbon/planning-tab/index.md#ribbon-planning-tab), which opens Planning first, open a small box to say what is wanted, in a sentence or a paragraph, whose request asks the harness, in a run of its own with no session, with the planning prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts), to break it into stories, each with a title, a prompt, and the mode that fits it. They come back as proposals, as the drafting and proposals say, each to be accepted, edited, or rejected, and none reaches the plan until it is accepted. An Ask answer's prompt cards also offer "Add to sprint", which adds the card's prompt as a story in its mode to Next sprint.

## Sprint

Stories move among Draft, the Backlog, and Next sprint by dragging, as the [DragReorderBehaviour](../../ui/behaviours/drag-reorder/index.md#drag-reorder-behaviour) says, a card dragged by its grip from one of them into a gap in another as within any one, the gap opened in the column the pointer is over, as motion says; an empty one takes a drop at its top. Dragged near the board's left or right edge, the board scrolls sideways, and near a column's top or bottom, that column scrolls, as dragging says. Only Draft, the Backlog, and Next sprint take drops: Current sprint and Done open no gap, a story dropped on them stays where it was, and their cards can't be picked up, nor can a finding. Stories move too from a card's menu: in Draft, "Move to backlog"; in the Backlog, "Move to next sprint" and "Move to draft"; in Next sprint, "Move to backlog". Their order within Next sprint is the order they will be sent. A card's menu also has "Duplicate" and "Delete".
"Send sprint", a primary button at the right of Next sprint's heading, enabled while it holds a story, sends every story in it, in order, as though each had been written in the chat input on its mode's tab and sent, one after another, as the [PromptSending](../prompt-mode/sending/index.md#prompt-sending) says: each task queues in its lane behind the one before it, in the order of the sprint, and each question runs at once. The stories go into the queue as one block, so nothing sent later comes between them, and the queue's auto-send carries them on as ever, as the [QueueList](../prompt-mode/queue-list/index.md#queue-list) says.
Each story starts a conversation of its own, as though New conversation had been pressed just before it, and so does each later step of a story's chain: a story never carries on the conversation of the story before it, nor of anything its lane ran before the sprint. New conversation, pressed before the sprint was sent, is left for the next prompt written in the chat input.
A story can't be sent on its own. The only way a story reaches work is through the sprint: a story in Draft or the Backlog waits until it is moved into Next sprint and the sprint is sent, a story in Draft never reaching a sprint without first moving to the Backlog or Next sprint, and a story in Next sprint goes when the sprint does. Nothing in Planning, its cards, their menus, the open story, the keyboard, the palette, or the ribbon, sends a single story, and nothing elsewhere sends a story by any other route: a story can't be dragged or copied into the chat input or the queue to be sent from there, and its menu has no "Send" or "Edit in chat input". The chat input's own prompts are not stories and are sent as ever; once a prompt is a story, the sprint is its only way to work. To send one story at once, it is the only story in Next sprint when Send sprint is pressed. A story that failed or was cancelled is sent again the same way, with the next sprint.
Sending the sprint moves its stories into the "Current sprint" column, to the right of Next sprint, so Next sprint is empty again and stories added meanwhile go there, to be the sprint after. Current sprint and Done are columns of the board whatever they hold, never appearing, disappearing, or collapsing; while no sprint is under way Current sprint is empty and shows its empty state, as Done does before anything is done. A story in Current sprint keeps its place, its card showing its task's status as it queues, runs, and ends, and clicking it opens its task in the Tasks tab; it can't be moved or edited there. Once every story of Current sprint has ended, its column's heading offers "Close sprint", which moves the stories that are done into the Done column, their cards muted, and those that failed, were cancelled, or stopped to the start of Next sprint, in their order, to be sent again. While a sprint is current, Send sprint is disabled, its tooltip saying a sprint is already under way.
Send sprint only ever moves into Current sprint the stories it actually sent. A story with nothing to send, its title and its prompt both empty, is skipped: it stays in Next sprint, where it was, and Send sprint's result says, muted, how many it skipped and why, as "1 empty story left in Next sprint". A sprint where every story is empty sends nothing and makes no Current sprint.
Once a sprint is done, it can always be closed. Every story of Current sprint counts as ended once its task has ended, done, failed, cancelled, or stopped, or once its task can no longer be found, as when its record was deleted, it was never recorded, or the application quit before it was. A story whose task is missing is never shown as Queued, or as anything still to come: its card reads "Task missing", muted, in the theme's warning colour, its tooltip saying its task can't be found, and it counts as ended and not Done. A story still waiting in its lane's queue, or held for review, as the paused section says, is still to come and hasn't ended. So Close sprint shows as soon as no story of Current sprint is building, compiling, running, paused, queued, or held, and never waits on a task that can't arrive.
Close sprint treats a story whose task is missing as it treats one that failed or was cancelled: it goes back to the start of Next sprint, with the others sent again, in their order, never into Done. Closing saves the sections, Done, Next sprint, the Backlog, Draft, and the emptied Current sprint, to `order.json` straight away, as the [ProjectData](../project-data/index.md#project-data) says, and Current sprint's state is worked out afresh from the stories' tasks whenever the plan is read, so a sprint that finished, or whose tasks went missing, before a reload or a restart can still be closed after it, as before.

## Motion

Dragging a card on the board feels as it does in Trello, and the board opens the gap, as the [DragReorderBehaviour](../../ui/behaviours/drag-reorder/index.md#drag-reorder-behaviour) lets its user do, in place of the accent line alone. Only the board's cards move this way; steps in an open story, and every other list, are dragged as the [DragReorderBehaviour](../../ui/behaviours/drag-reorder/index.md#drag-reorder-behaviour) says, with its line.
A card picked up by its grip lifts off the board as a full-size copy of itself, the same width and height, drawn as the parts draw a story card, tilted a few degrees, about 3, on the theme's overlay surface with its edge border and the soft shadow the [Theme](../../ui/theme/index.md#theme)'s elevation gives floating surfaces, the one shadow on the board. It follows the pointer, held where it was grabbed, and never takes the mouse. The card's own place in its column becomes the gap it left, empty, the card's height, so the column doesn't jump as it lifts.
Where the card would land, the cards slide apart to open a placeholder the dragged card's height, 8 pixels from the cards either side, as the cards are spaced: a box the card's size on the theme's well surface, with its corners rounded 6 pixels as a card's are, and no border, so it reads as an empty slot. The gap is chosen as the [DragReorderBehaviour](../../ui/behaviours/drag-reorder/index.md#drag-reorder-behaviour) chooses it, among the cards of the column the pointer is over, and only one is open at a time: as the pointer moves into another gap, or another column, the gap it left closes as the new one opens, and the gap the card came from closes once the pointer leaves its column, opening again if it comes back. A column that takes no drops opens no gap, and its cards never move while a card is dragged over it.
Nothing waits on motion while the user is waiting on it. The gap the card would drop into is updated at once, the moment the pointer crosses the middle of a card, exactly as the [DragReorderBehaviour](../../ui/behaviours/drag-reorder/index.md#drag-reorder-behaviour) says, and a drop always goes where the gap was chosen, even while the cards are still sliding toward it; only the sliding of the cards around it is animated, quickly, as below.
Dropped over an open gap, the copy settles into it: it straightens, its shadow fades, and it moves from where it was released into the placeholder, which it then is, the story saved in its new place at the moment of the drop, as every change to the plan is. Dropped anywhere else, or where it began, it settles back into the gap it came from the same way, and nothing changes. Escape while dragging cancels it, settling the card back where it was.
A card moved any other way animates to its new place, as Linear's do, in a quick motion of about 150 milliseconds, eased out, sliding from where it was to where it now is, the cards it passes or leaves sliding to close and open the room it takes, never fading or bouncing. That covers every move the sprint describes: "Move to next sprint", "Move to backlog", and "Move to draft" from a card's menu, or the bulk bar, Alt+Up, Alt+Down, Alt+Left, and Alt+Right, Ctrl+Enter, Send sprint moving its stories into Current sprint, and Close sprint moving them into Done and back to the start of Next sprint. A card added, as by a composer or Duplicate, slides the cards below it down to make room, and a card deleted slides them up to close it, in the same motion. The board scrolls sideways, and a column up or down, to keep a moved card that has focus in view, as the keyboard says. Focus goes with the card at once, not when its motion ends, and the plan is saved at once.
The side panel slides in from the board's right as it opens, in the same quick motion, the board narrowing alongside it, and slides back out to the right as it closes, the board widening as it goes; replacing what it holds with another story, drafting, or research changes its content in place, with no slide. Its content, and focus in it, are there as soon as it starts to open.
The open story's card is kept in view, however the board changes around it. As the side panel opens and the board narrows, the board scrolls sideways alongside it, in the same quick motion, just enough to keep the open story's card fully in view, when it was fully in view before; a card already partly out of view is left where it is. A story opened from anywhere outside the board, as a proposal's "Added to Backlog" or "Added to <story>" link, or a palette or ribbon action that opens one, scrolls the board sideways and its column up or down, in the same motion, just enough that its card is fully in view, then highlights it as the open story. Clicking a card only partly in view opens it and scrolls the board and its column just enough to show it all; a card already fully in view never scrolls anything. Each scroll moves only as far as it must, the card landing at the nearest edge of the view, never centred.
Nothing above the view moves what is in it. In a column scrolled away from its top, a card above the view that is added, deleted, or changes height, as a story's status or step lines arriving in Current sprint, or a sprint closing and its stories leaving, never moves the cards in view: the column's scroll shifts by the same amount, at once and with no motion, so they stay exactly where they were, and the column's thumb moves without jumping, as the [Scrollbar.steadiness](../../ui/components/scrollbar/index.md#steadiness) says. A column at its top keeps its top, and cards in view move as the motion above says.
Every motion here takes about 150 milliseconds, never longer, and a move made while another is still under way starts from wherever the card is then, never queued behind it.

## Auto Start

Next sprint can start on its own: a "Start automatically" switch on Next sprint's heading, beside Send sprint, its tooltip saying the next sprint starts as soon as the current one is done. It starts off, and is saved with the plan, in `order.json`, so it is kept across reloads and restarts.
While it is on, once every story of Current sprint has ended Done, the current sprint closes by itself, as Close sprint closes it, and Next sprint, if it holds a story, is sent at once, as Send sprint sends it, with nobody having to start it; and while no sprint is current, a story added to an empty Next sprint starts it the same way. A sprint that ended with a story failed, cancelled, stopped, or with its task missing, never starts the next by itself: it waits, Close sprint offered as ever, and the switch's row says, in the theme's warning colour, why the next didn't start. Nor does the next start while planning is paused, as the paused section says: it starts once the pause is ended by Resume, or Approve, if the switch is still on. An empty Next sprint starts nothing.
Each time a sprint starts by itself, a passive notification says so, "Next sprint started: 4 stories", with a link that opens Planning, and the debug log records it. Turning the switch off never stops a sprint already sent; it only keeps the next from starting by itself. Turning it on while no sprint is current and Next sprint holds a story starts Next sprint at once, as adding a story to it would, unless planning is paused.
The switch works while Planning isn't open, from the plan as saved, whichever tab is shown. When the project is opened, or the application starts, with the switch on, no sprint current, and Next sprint holding a story, it doesn't start by itself; the switch's row says, muted, "Waiting to start", with a "Start now" button, so a sprint never begins unseen as the application opens. A current sprint whose stories were cut off when the application quit, as every run is, ended them, and never starts the next by itself.
While the switch is on, Next sprint's heading shows "Auto" beside its count, in the theme's accent, and the ribbon's Send Sprint button's tooltip says the next sprint starts automatically.

## Saving

The stories, their order, and which section each is in are saved with the project's data, as the [ProjectData](../project-data/index.md#project-data) says, in `.suspense/planning/`, a file per story, holding its hidden anchor as a queued prompt's is, and an `order.json` listing the sections, Draft, the Backlog, Next sprint, Current sprint, and Done, and their stories in order, so the plan is kept with the project and comes back as it was left. A plan saved before Draft existed, its `order.json` with no Draft section, loads as it was with Draft empty, and is saved with one the next time the plan is. A story's steps are saved in its own file, in their order, as its steps say, never apart from it.

## Steps

A story can have steps: one or more further prompts, each a piece of the story done after the one before, as a chain's steps are. Each step has a prompt, a mode of its own, Code or Spec, starting as the story's, and a model and effort, starting as the story's, and may have attachments. A story with no steps is just its own prompt, as before; its prompt is always its first step.
An open story lists its steps beneath its prompt, in order, each a row numbered from 2, the story's own prompt being 1, with its mode pill and the first line of its prompt, opening in place to edit, as a story does. "Add step", beneath the last, adds one at the end, open and focused; several can be added one after another, Enter in an empty step's prompt adding none. Steps are reordered by dragging, as the [DragReorderBehaviour](../../ui/behaviours/drag-reorder/index.md#drag-reorder-behaviour) says, or Alt+Up and Alt+Down, and each has a remove button in its row and in its menu. The story's own prompt stays first and can't be moved among them.
A step belongs to its story and to nothing else. It is saved in the story's file, in a `steps` list of the story's hidden anchor, in its order, and saved as every change to the plan is, straight away; a story duplicated copies its steps, and one deleted deletes them. Its order is kept wherever the story goes, between sections, into a sprint, and back from Done.
Wherever the story is shown, its steps are too: its card in Planning shows how many beneath its title, muted, as "3 steps", with the list in its tooltip; the open story lists them as above; a proposal to add to it shows them, so what it would add to can be seen; and once it is sent, it is sent as a chain, its prompt first and each step after it in order, each step sent only once the one before it finishes, as the [PromptEditor](../prompt-mode/index.md#prompt-editor)'s chained tasks are, so the Tasks tab shows the story as one chain with its steps beneath it. A story sent can't be given more steps; its steps, sent or still to come, read as they were sent. In Current sprint, a story with steps lists its steps on its card, beneath its title, a line for each step, in order, each with its number, the first line of its prompt cut off with an ellipsis, and its own status, as a running chain's are in the Tasks tab; in Done, and in a finding started from the story, its steps are listed the same way, collapsed to its step count until it is expanded. The same steps, in the same order, are what every place shows, since every place reads them from the story's own file.
A step is only ever added to a story that exists. Adding one to a story that doesn't, as one deleted while a proposal naming it waited, or by another window, or whose file was removed from `.suspense/planning/` meanwhile, changes nothing: no story is made for it, no other story is given it, and nothing is saved. It says so in plain words where it was asked for, as "That story no longer exists, so the step wasn't added", in the theme's error colour, as the states say, with what was to be added kept, so it can be added to another story or as a new one. A step added to a story already sent is refused the same way, saying the story has been sent.

## Layout

Everything in Planning is laid out on one rhythm, so the board scans at a glance. The board fills the body beneath the tab bar, with 24 pixels of padding at its top, sides, and foot. Its columns are all the same fixed width, 320 pixels, 16 pixels apart, each as tall as the board, set side by side from its left edge in the order work moves, Draft, the first, Backlog, Next sprint, Current sprint, Done, and Findings, the last. Each column is a list, as Trello draws one: a container of its own, as the parts draw a list, on the theme's recessed surface, one step from the base the board is on, its corners rounded 8 pixels, with its heading and its cards inside it, and no border. Three things set a list apart from the board's base, all quieter than any card's state: its recessed surface; the theme's pressed bevel around it, inside its rounded corners, so it reads as sunk into the base; and the 16 pixel gaps between columns. Each column also has a look of its own, telling it from its neighbours: a 2 pixel edge along the list's top, inside its rounded corners and above its heading, in the colour its status icon uses, as the parts give it, laid over the recessed surface at 50%, so Draft's is tertiary text, as the Backlog's is, the two told apart by their icons, Next sprint's secondary text, Current sprint's the accent, Done's success, and Findings' secondary text. The edge is the only place a column's colour shows besides its icon: its heading, its name, its cards, its empty state, and the drag placeholder keep their own surfaces and colours untouched, the placeholder its well surface. Laid over at half strength and 2 pixels tall, a column's edge is always quieter than a card's hover, its selected surface, its focus ring, or the open story's 3 pixel accent line, as the Theme's hierarchy orders decoration below state.
Each column's heading reads as Linear heads a group: a row 32 pixels tall at the list's top, holding, from its left, the column's status icon, 14 pixels, as the parts give it; its name in small semibold text, in the theme's primary text colour; its count beside it, muted; and its actions at its right, each a labelled button, never an icon alone, as the sections give them: "Draft stories" and "Research" on the Backlog; "Send sprint" and "Start automatically" on Next sprint; "Close sprint" on Current sprint, once its sprint can close. A heading with more actions than fit its width wraps them onto a second line beneath its name rather than cutting any off; Draft's heading has no actions but its "+ Add". On Draft, the Backlog, and Next sprint, hovering the heading, or focus anywhere in it, shows "+ Add" just after its count, a small ghost button with a plus icon and its label, never the icon alone, its tooltip saying it adds a story at the top of the list; it takes its room in the heading whether shown or not, so the heading's actions never shift as it appears, and the other columns' headings have none. 8 pixels beneath the heading come its cards, one beneath another, 8 pixels apart, each the list's full inner width.
At the foot of Draft, of the Backlog, and of Next sprint, 8 pixels beneath its last card, or beneath its empty state, is its "Add story" line: a row 32 pixels tall, the list's full inner width, with a plus icon and the label "Add story" in small muted text, its corners rounded 6 pixels, and no border; hovered, it takes the theme's hover surface and its text the theme's primary text colour. It scrolls with the cards, after the last of them. Its composer, as creating says, is drawn where it was clicked, at the foot in the line's place, or at the top, above the first card, from "+ Add": a story card, as the parts draw one, its title a text box in the card's title text, with the focus ring around the card, and beneath it, muted, "Enter to add, Escape to cancel"; the cards below it move down to make room, and the list scrolls to keep it in view. Current sprint, Done, and Findings have no "Add story" line.
Each column scrolls up and down on its own, its heading staying at its top while its cards scroll beneath it, inside the list's rounded corners, with the [Scrollbar](../../ui/components/scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar) shown along the list's right, inside it, while it holds more than fits. The board scrolls sideways when its columns are wider than the tab, with the [Scrollbar](../../ui/components/scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar) along its foot; while they fit, it doesn't scroll. The wheel and the trackpad scroll what is under the pointer, each part of the board on its own. A vertical wheel turn or two-finger swipe over a column, its heading included, scrolls only that column up or down; it never scrolls the board sideways, and it never passes on to the board, not when the column is at its top or its end, nor when it has nothing to scroll. Shift with the wheel, a sideways trackpad swipe, or a mouse's horizontal wheel, tilted or a thumb wheel, anywhere on the board, over a column, its heading, or the padding and gaps around them, scrolls the board sideways while its columns are wider than the tab, and does nothing while they fit. The horizontal wheel never scrolls a column up or down, and it moves the board the way it is turned, right moving the board right and left moving it left. A vertical wheel turn over the board outside every column, on its padding, in the 16 pixel gaps between columns, or in the space beside the last column, scrolls the board sideways instead, as Trello does, down moving it right and up left. A diagonal trackpad swipe over a column scrolls the column up or down and the board sideways together, each by its own share of the swipe, the up and down share to the column and the sideways share to the board. Scrolling over the side panel, the pause bar, or the bulk bar never moves the board or any of its columns: the side panel scrolls only itself, and the two bars scroll nothing. Every card's state reads the same way, as below, and every label is the same small text, muted where it is secondary.
The board is kept as it was left while Planning's tab stays open, as the [Body](../application/Body.md#body) keeps a tab. Selecting another tab and then Planning's again shows the board scrolled sideways exactly where it was left, and every column scrolled up or down exactly where it was, at once, with nothing animating, sliding, or scrolling into view, as though the tab had never been left; nothing is scrolled to its start or to a card on the way back. The side panel opening or closing in the meantime, as a story opened from outside the board, changes only the board's sideways scroll, as far as the panel's opening or closing needs, as motion says, and shows it already settled when the tab is back; every column keeps its own scroll through it. The scroll is the board's own, kept only while its tab is open, and never saved with the plan, in `order.json` or anywhere else: closing Planning's tab and opening it again, or reloading the window, starts the board at its left edge and every column at its top.
The side panel is the one place anything opens: an open story, Draft stories, and Research, never beneath a heading or a card, and never in a popup or over the board. A composer is not an opened story but a card being written, and is the one thing drawn in a list, where its story will sit. It is docked at the right of Planning's tab, 400 pixels wide, as tall as the tab, from the tab bar down to the bottom of the body, a 1 pixel line in the theme's line colour along its left edge, and it scrolls up and down on its own, its heading staying at its top, with the [Scrollbar](../../ui/components/scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar) along its right while it holds more than fits. Only one thing is in it at a time: opening a story, drafting, or research replaces whatever it held, and closing it leaves nothing there. While it is open the board narrows to the space left of it, its columns keeping their width and scrolling sideways as ever when they no longer fit; the panel never covers the board, and the board never covers it. Closed, it takes no space and the board fills the tab again. It slides in and out at the right, as motion says.
While paused, the pause bar runs across the top of the whole board, above every column, as the paused section says, beside the side panel when it is open, never over it. Each column is headed as above, so nothing sits outside the rhythm, and an open story, a drafting or research panel, and the citations and steps inside a story all use the same five parts, below.

## Parts

Everything in Planning is built from five parts, each always drawn the same way, in the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode:
- A list: one per column, as the layout places it, 320 pixels wide and as tall as the board, on the theme's recessed surface, one step from the base, with no border, the theme's pressed bevel inside its edges, its corners rounded 8 pixels, 8 pixels of padding; a 2 pixel edge along its top, in its status icon's colour laid over the recessed surface at 50%, as the layout says, the column's one look of its own; its heading row at its top, as the layout says, then its cards, or its empty state centred beneath its heading; its heading's status icon one per column, each always the same: Draft a pencil in the theme's tertiary text colour, a drawn glyph and never a circle, so it can't be mistaken for the Backlog's; the Backlog a dashed circle in the theme's tertiary text colour; Next sprint an empty circle in the theme's secondary text colour; Current sprint a half-filled circle in the theme's accent; Done a filled circle with a check in the theme's success colour; and Findings a magnifying glass in the theme's secondary text colour; each, with the list's top edge in its colour, telling its column apart at a glance while still only repeating the column's name, never standing for it alone
- A story card: a box the full inner width of its list, on the theme's raised surface, with a 1 pixel line in the theme's line colour, corners rounded 6 pixels, 8 pixels of padding above and below and 10 at its sides, 8 pixels from the next; a top line with its drag grip, 16 pixels, in the theme's tertiary text colour, at its left, its title beside it, the card's primary text, in up to two lines, cut off with an ellipsis after the second, and its menu button at its right on hover and always while it is focused; beneath the title, 4 pixels below it, a single property row, 20 pixels tall, in small muted text, of small items 8 pixels apart: its mode pill, in its mode's colour, as the PromptModes colours it, its step count, its attachment icon, each when it has them, and its status and time, right-aligned, once it has been sent; and, in Current sprint, its steps' lines beneath, as its steps say; used for every story, in every column, muted in Done. Its states are three distinct steps, as the Theme's hierarchy orders them: hovering raises it one surface step, to the theme's hover surface; the open story keeps a 3 pixel line in the theme's accent along its left edge, as the stories say, whether or not it is hovered; a selected card, as the selection below says, takes the theme's selected surface in place of its raised one, hovered or not; and focus shows the theme's focus ring, in the accent, 2 pixels around it, over any of them, so a hover is always quieter than a selection, and a selection than focus, as the Theme orders them, and the open story's line, an edge rather than a surface, reads apart from both, a card being open, selected, and focused at once without any of the three hiding another
- A row: 36 pixels tall, for steps in an open story and for findings; its secondary text muted and cut off with an ellipsis, its buttons small ghost buttons with labels, shown at its right on hover and always while it is focused
- A panel: the side panel, docked at the board's right, full height, as the layout places it, on the theme's raised surface, its corners square, 12 pixels of padding, a heading row of 32 pixels with its name, as "Draft stories", "Research", or the story's title, and its close button, its content beneath, and its actions in a footer row, right-aligned, the primary action last; used for an open story, drafting, and research
- A card: a box inside a panel, on the theme's base surface, with a 1 pixel line in the theme's line colour, corners rounded 4 pixels, 12 pixels of padding, 8 pixels from the next; a label row at its top, its content, and a footer row of labelled buttons; used for proposals and for each finding's summary
Labels are words, never icons alone: every button reads what it does, "Accept", "Send sprint", "Start automatically", and an icon beside a label only repeats it. Each heading's count is a plain number, muted, and each status a coloured label, as the states say. The pause bar is a row across the whole board's top, above its columns, 40 pixels tall, its text and buttons on one line, the same height whatever it says.
Stories are selected as Linear selects issues, to be acted on together. Only a story in Draft, the Backlog, or Next sprint can be selected, the three lists that take moves, as the sprint says; a card in Current sprint or Done, and a finding, never is. Ctrl+click (Cmd+click on macOS) on a card toggles it alone in or out of the selection, the rest kept; Shift+click selects the range within its column from the card last clicked or toggled there to the clicked one, inclusive, added to the selection, or the clicked card alone when nothing in that column was clicked or toggled yet; and X toggles one from the keyboard, as the keyboard says. A selection can hold stories from all three lists at once. A plain click opens the story in the side panel as ever, and leaves the selection as it is. Selected cards show the theme's selected surface, as the story card above says, distinct from focus and from the open story's line. The selection is the board's own, never saved with the plan: a selected story leaves it when it is deleted or leaves Draft, the Backlog, and Next sprint, as when the sprint it is in is sent.
While any card is selected, the bulk bar runs across the board's foot, beneath its columns, beside the side panel when it is open, never over it nor over the board: a row 40 pixels tall, on the theme's raised surface with a 1 pixel line in the theme's line colour along its top, the columns shortening to make room as it slides up in motion's quick motion, and lengthening again as it slides away once nothing is selected. At its left it names how many are selected, as "3 selected"; at its right, labelled buttons, never icons alone, in this order: "Move to next sprint", which moves the selected stories in the Backlog to the end of Next sprint; "Move to backlog", which moves those in Draft and in Next sprint to the end of the Backlog; "Move to draft", which moves those in the Backlog to the end of Draft; "Change mode", which opens a mode picker above it, the one a card's pill opens, setting the mode of every selected story to the one picked, their steps keeping their own; "Duplicate", which duplicates each, every copy just beneath its original, as a card's menu does; "Delete", which deletes them all after one confirmation naming how many, as "Delete 3 stories?"; and "Clear", which empties the selection. Every move keeps the stories' order, as the selection orders them, Draft's first, top to bottom, then the Backlog's, then Next sprint's, and animates as motion says; a move button is disabled, its tooltip saying why, while none of the selection is in the list it moves from. Moved stories stay selected, duplicates are not selected, and the originals stay so. The bar has no Send and sends nothing: a story still reaches work only through the sprint, as the sprint says.
Dragging a selected card by its grip carries the whole selection, in its order: the other selected cards leave their places as it lifts, their columns closing up, and the lifted copy is the grabbed card, as motion draws it, with the cards it carries stacked a few pixels behind it and their count beside its title. The gap opens as tall as the cards together, 8 pixels apart, and dropped there they settle into it in their order, all in that list, saved at once; dropped anywhere else, or cancelled with Escape, they all settle back where they were. Dragging a card that isn't selected moves it alone and leaves the selection as it is.
Right-clicking a card opens its menu at the pointer, the same menu its hover button opens, with the same items, acting on that card alone, in place of the browser's own; it closes as that menu does, Escape among the ways.

## States

Each part of Planning has the same few states, shown the same way wherever they come up, so a state is never guessed from what is missing.
- Empty: a single muted line, centred in the column beneath its heading, saying what is missing and what to do, as "Nothing planned. Drag stories here, or press Ctrl+N.", with no illustration
- Loading: a spinner and a short muted label of what is happening, as "Drafting stories…", in the place the result will appear, never a blank space
- Paused: a story whose task is paused shows "Paused" as its status, in the theme's warning colour, with a small pause icon, and a "Resume" button on its card, as the PromptSending says of pausing; a sprint with any story paused says so in its heading, as "1 paused", in the same colour
- Error: a line in the theme's error colour, saying what went wrong in plain words, with what the harness or the application reported beneath it collapsed under "Details", and a "Try again" button where trying again can help
A story's status on its card is the same coloured label a task has, as the [MessageList](../prompt-mode/message-list/index.md#message-list)'s status says, Queued, Running with its spinner and time, Done, Failed, Cancelled, Paused, or, where its task can't be found, Task missing, as the sprint says, and a story not yet sent shows nothing there, so its absence means "not sent".
Each part shows each state that can come up for it, worded for it:
- Story list: empty, "Nothing planned. Press Ctrl+N to add a story." in Next sprint, "No drafts. Jot an idea down here." in Draft, "Nothing waiting." in the Backlog, "No sprint under way. Send sprint to start one." in Current sprint, and "Nothing done yet." in Done; loading, while the plan is read on opening, a few skeleton cards in each column, never an empty column; error, when the plan can't be read or saved, saying which file and why, with "Try again"
- Research and its findings: loading, the live line of what it is reading with its spinner; empty, "No findings yet." in Findings; error, the run's failure with "Try again", which keeps the question in its box; a finding that ended early, as stopped, marked "Incomplete", muted, in its row
- Pause: the pause bar, in the theme's warning colour, as the paused section says, and the sprint's Send buttons disabled with their tooltips saying why; a sprint that can't start for a failed story says so in its heading, in the same colour
- Proposals: loading, the drafting line and spinner; empty, "No stories proposed." with "Draft again"; error, the run's failure with "Try again"; a proposal with no spec cited, in the warning colour with "Draft again", as the spec grounding says

## Drafting

Drafting stories shows its work in one place, the side panel, docked at the board's right, as the layout places it, replacing whatever it held, never in a popup that hides the list. It has the request box at its top, labelled "Describe what you want", and beneath it, while the run goes, its research: a muted line of what the harness is doing, as "Reading the spec…", with its spinner, updating as it goes, and a "Stop" button. Once it ends, the panel lists its proposals, as below, then "Accept all" and "Reject all" buttons along the panel's foot, and closes itself once none is left to decide. A run that fails shows its error, as the states say, and leaves the request in its box to try again; one that proposes nothing says so, as an empty state. Proposals are kept until each is decided, so closing Planning and coming back finds them as they were.
Drafting can also be started from an open story, with "Ask agent" in its card's menu or the open story's footer: the request box then reads "What does this story need?", the run is told the story's title and prompt, and the drafting panel takes the open story's place in the side panel, the story's card staying highlighted while the draft is about it.
The request is sent with the panel's "Draft" button, its primary action, or by pressing Enter in the request box, whichever label it reads; Ctrl+Enter there starts it too, and the button's tooltip gives Enter as its shortcut. Shift+Enter adds a new line in the box and sends nothing. A request that is empty, or only spaces and new lines, starts nothing, and the button is disabled while it is. While a run is going, Enter starts no second one, and the button is disabled. Enter in the request box only ever sends the request: the list's Enter, opening or closing the focused story, never fires while focus is in the box.

## Proposals

The agent never writes the plan itself. Its run is a Question run, as the [Sandbox](../sandbox/index.md#sandbox) says, able to read the project and change nothing, and Suspense data is never granted to it, so it can't touch `.suspense/planning/`; it only proposes, and nothing it proposes reaches the plan until the user accepts it.
Each proposal is one concrete task, with a title, a prompt, and the mode that fits it, and says where it should go: either "New story", to become a story of its own, or "Add to" a story, naming an existing story the run was shown, the open story first, to be added to it. The planning prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts) asks for each proposal as a fenced block whose info string is `suspense-story`, holding its title, its mode, its target, `new` or the story's id, its `spec` list of citations into the Piton source, as the spec grounding says, and its prompt, so the application reads it whatever else the reply says. The planning prompt explains the form with an example, as:
```suspense-story
title: Close a finished sprint
mode: chain
target: new
spec:
- spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint: when Close sprint shows
- No match: archiving a closed sprint
prompt:
Close sprint is offered once every story of the current sprint has
ended, as spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint says.
```
A block that names a story that no longer exists is shown as "New story", with a muted note saying so.

## Spec Grounding

A drafted story is grounded in the project's spec, never written from the request alone. Before proposing, the drafter searches the spec for what each story touches: the requirements and behaviours it changes or relies on, the names it uses, as a feature, a component, or a property, and the sections they are in. It reads the spec as every run does, from its compiled reference or from what `piton slice` prints, never from the Piton source, as the [ModeSystemPrompts](../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts) says, and the planning prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts) tells it to.
Each proposal cites what it found, specifically: its `suspense-story` block holds a `spec` list, one entry per element, each a link to the element in the spec's Piton source, under the spec location, never to the compiled reference: the .pi file, relative to the project directory, then `#` and the element it names, an anchor or a property on one, in the form `piton slice` takes, as `spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint`, with a short line of what in it the story touches. The story's prompt names those elements and links to them in the same form. Only elements the drafter found are cited, and where they point is the only thing that is Piton source: the drafter still learns what the spec says only from the compiled reference or from what `piton slice` prints, never by reading the Piton source, as the [ModeSystemPrompts](../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts) says, and works out each element's source from what `piton slice` prints for it, which names the file each declaration is in.
The application checks each link against the Piton source when the proposal arrives: the file has to exist under the spec location, and has to define the named element, the anchor declared in it and, for a property, that property on it, as `piton slice` would find it. A link that fails either check is dropped, with a muted note on the card saying which link it dropped and why, "no such file" or "the file doesn't define Planning.sprint". Each citation, on the proposal card and in an accepted story's "Spec" list, opens that place in the Piton source, the file in the editor at the element's declaration, as the [OpenFile](../open-file/index.md#open-file) opens a file.
Where no spec element matches part of a story, as a request for something the spec doesn't describe yet, the story says so instead of inventing one: its `spec` list holds an entry reading "No match", with what was looked for, and its prompt says plainly that the spec has nothing on it yet, so the change is new. A proposal with no element at all, and no "No match", isn't shown as a story: its card says the drafter cited no spec, in the theme's warning colour, with "Draft again", which runs the draft for that story once more.
The citations are shown on the proposal's card, beneath its prompt, as a short list, each element's name, as `Planning.sprint`, and its file, muted, as a link that opens that place in the Piton source, a "No match" entry muted with a small marker, and are kept with the story once it is accepted, listed in the open story beneath its steps as "Spec", and shown in its card's tooltip. They can be edited with the story, removed, or added to by hand: "Add citation" opens a picker of the spec's elements, its anchors and their properties, found from the Piton source and searched by name, never from the compiled reference, and adds the one picked in the same form, checked as a proposal's are.
Each citation says what kind of element it is, "Requirement", "Behaviour", "Name", or "Section", shown as a small muted label before it, and quotes the few words of the spec it rests on, so what the story relies on can be checked at a glance. Grounding holds for every proposal, however it came: from Draft stories, from research that ends with proposals, and from an Ask answer's `suspense-story` block, each checked and flagged the same way when it arrives.

## Proposal Cards

Each proposal is a card in the panel, in the order given: a label at its top, "New story" in the theme's accent, or, for an addition, "Add to this story" where it targets the story the research or draft was started from, and "Add to" and the story's title otherwise, in the story's own mode's colour, so where it will go is always read before anything else on the card; its title, its mode pill, and its prompt beneath, clipped at four lines with "Read more"; and three buttons along its foot, "Accept", "Edit", and "Reject", reachable by Tab and labelled for a screen reader. Edit opens the card's title, prompt, mode, and target in place, the target a menu of "New story" and each story, to be changed before it is accepted; editing doesn't accept it. Reject removes the card, with a short "Undo" in its place for a few seconds.
Accept records it in the plan straight away, saved as any change to the plan is: a new story goes into the Backlog, at its end, in its mode, marked "From agent" with a small sparkle beside its title until it is first opened, its spec citations kept with it, whether it was accepted on its own card or with "Accept all", and whether it came from drafting, research, or an Ask answer. Accepting never adds anything to Next sprint, so it never starts a sprint, however Start automatically is set; an accepted story reaches a sprint only once it is moved to Next sprint, as the sprint says; an addition is added to the named story as a new step at its end, as its steps say, its attachments with it, and the story is marked "Updated by agent" until it is next opened, the new step shown highlighted the first time it is; where the story no longer exists by then, the step isn't added, as the steps say, and the card stays, its target changed to "New story", to be accepted again. A story already sent can't be added to: its proposals offer only "New story". Each card, once decided, goes from the panel, and an accepted one leaves a one-line muted note in its place, "Added to Backlog" or "Added to <story>", with a link that opens the story where it is, in the Backlog or its section.
Ask answers can propose the same way: a `suspense-story` block in an answer is shown as a proposal card, with the same Accept, Edit, and Reject, its accepting recording it in the plan as above, so a story can come out of a conversation without anything written silently.

## Research

The agent can be asked to research a topic before anything is planned or built: "Research", a button beside "Draft stories" on the Backlog's heading, Research on the [RibbonPlanningTab](../../ui/components/ribbon/planning-tab/index.md#ribbon-planning-tab), which opens Planning first, and "Research" in an open story's menu, open a box labelled "What should be looked into?". Research runs as a read-only investigation, a Question run, as the [Sandbox](../sandbox/index.md#sandbox) says, which can read the project and the web and change nothing, given the research prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts), which asks for findings, not changes: what was found, where, with links to the files and lines it read, what it is unsure of, and what it would suggest, and it may end with proposals, as the proposals say. Its box and its run are shown in the side panel, replacing whatever it held, as drafting's are, its live line of what it is reading, a Stop button, and its spinner, and its proposals in the same cards with the same buttons as drafting's, with Accept all and Reject all at its foot.
Its findings are a document of their own, "Research: <topic>", rendered as markdown with its links clickable, shown in the Findings column, the board's last, after Done, newest first, each a row with its topic, when it ran, and its state, and opening in a body tab of its own to read whole. Findings started from a story are also listed in that story, beneath its steps. They are saved with the plan, in `.suspense/planning/research/`, a markdown file each, so they can be read again later, and can be deleted from their row's menu.

## Paused

Once research ends, however it ended, planning is paused. While it is paused nothing is implemented: Send sprint, the ribbon's Send Sprint, and the sprint's Ctrl+Shift+Enter are disabled, their tooltips saying planning is paused for review, and no proposal from the research is added to the plan by itself. Stories can still be written, edited, ordered, and moved, and proposals still accepted or rejected one by one, since those only change the plan.
Nothing of the plan starts while it is paused, not only nothing new: a story of Current sprint still waiting in the queue, not yet started, is held where it is, as a queued prompt being edited is held, as the [QueueList](../prompt-mode/queue-list/index.md#queue-list) says, its card reading "Held for review", muted, and its lane waits on it; a story already running when the pause began runs on to its end, since stopping it would leave its work half done, and the bar says how many are still running. A chain's next step, as a story's steps are sent, is held the same way. Once the pause ends, by Resume or Approve, what was held goes on in its order, as though nothing had stopped it.
The pause is plain to see: a bar across the top of the whole board, above every column, in the theme's warning colour, with a pause icon, reads "Paused for review", names the research it is waiting on, with a link that opens its findings, and holds two buttons, "Resume", which ends the pause, and "Approve and send sprint", which ends it and sends Next sprint at once. The Planning tab in the body shows a small pause icon beside its name, and the ribbon's Planning tab a warning dot, while it is paused. Pressing either button is the only way the pause ends; nothing the agent does, and no time passing, ends it. A second research while paused keeps the pause, naming the latest.
The pause is saved with the plan, in `order.json`, with the research it waits on, as soon as it begins, so it is still paused, and still shown so, after the project is closed and opened again, the application restarted, or the window reloaded, until it is resumed or approved.

## Keyboard

Everything in Planning can be done from the keyboard. Tab moves through the columns' heading buttons, "+ Add" among them on Draft, the Backlog, and Next sprint, the cards and rows, each list's "Add story" line after its last card, and the open story's fields in order, and the focused one shows the theme's focus ring. In a column, Up and Down move between its cards and rows, as J and K do, J down and K up, Down or J from the last reaching its "Add story" line, where Enter opens the composer, and Left and Right move focus to the column beside it, onto its card or row nearest the focused one's height, skipping a column with none, and scrolling the board sideways to show it; Enter opens or closes the focused story, A accepts the focused proposal, E edits it, and R rejects it. Alt+Up and Alt+Down move the focused story up or down within its column, and Alt+Left and Alt+Right move it into the column beside it, as dragging does, where that column takes it: from Draft Alt+Right moves it to the end of the Backlog; from the Backlog Alt+Left moves it to the end of Draft and Alt+Right to the end of Next sprint; and from Next sprint Alt+Left moves it to the end of the Backlog, focus going with it; Alt+Left in Draft, the first column, does nothing; anywhere else, as a story in Current sprint or Done, or toward a column that takes no drops, they do nothing. Ctrl+N (Cmd+N on macOS) opens the composer at the foot of the list that has focus, Draft, the Backlog, or Next sprint, when focus is on its heading, one of its cards, or its "Add story" line, and at the foot of Next sprint otherwise, as when focus is in Current sprint, Done, Findings, the side panel, or nowhere on the board, scrolling the board sideways to show it. In a composer, Enter adds the story and opens the next composer beneath it, focus moving to its title, and Escape discards it, focus going back to what opened it, the "Add story" line or the heading's "+ Add". Ctrl+Enter moves the focused story to Next sprint, or to the Backlog from it or from Draft, Ctrl+Shift+Enter sends the sprint, and M opens the focused story's mode picker, whose options are picked with the arrow keys and Enter. Delete deletes the focused story after a confirmation. X toggles the focused story in or out of the selection, as the parts say. While no card has focus, the shortcuts that act on one story, Enter, X, M, Ctrl+Enter, Delete, and the Alt arrows, act on the card under the pointer instead, as Linear's do, without moving focus to it, and do nothing when the pointer is over no card; with a card focused, they act on it, wherever the pointer is. None of them sends a story, as the sprint says. Escape closes what is open, a composer, a menu, the selection, cleared before anything else closes, then the side panel, whether it holds a story, drafting, or research, one at a time. Every button and control has a label a screen reader reads, as its visible text or, for an icon, its tooltip, and each shortcut is given in the tooltip of the control it stands for.
Ctrl+Shift+D opens Draft stories, focusing its request box, where Enter starts the draft, as Ctrl+Enter also does, and Shift+Enter adds a new line; Ctrl+Shift+R opens Research, focusing its box, where Ctrl+Enter starts it; F6 moves focus between the board's regions, the pause bar, each column, the bulk bar while it is shown, the side panel when it is open, and back, so each is a single stop; within the pause bar, Tab reaches Resume and Approve and send sprint; within the bulk bar, Tab reaches its buttons in order; within an open story, Tab reaches its steps, its Add step, and its Spec citations, each citation opening on Enter; and within Findings, Enter opens the focused finding in its tab. The Start automatically switch is reached by Tab on Next sprint's heading and toggled with Space. Focus never lands on something hidden or disabled, and after an action it stays where it was or moves to what the action made, as the new story or the next proposal, never back to the top.

content.text:
I've added the Draft column to the Planning board in `src/planning.rs`. **None of it has been compiled or tested.** `cargo` stops on `include_str!` of the prompt files in `.suspense/system-prompts/`, which this environment can't read, so it never type-checks `planning.rs`. A scratch copy didn't work either, because `/tmp` isn't writable. Please run `cargo test` on your side.

What changed:
- **The column:** Draft is the first column, with a pencil icon (`IconName::Pencil`) in tertiary text and the same tertiary top edge as the Backlog. Its heading has only "+ Add", and its empty state reads "No drafts. Jot an idea down here."
- **Writing stories:** the "Add story" line, "+ Add" and Ctrl+N all work in Draft. Accepted proposals still go only into the Backlog, and the Backlog's "Draft stories" button is unchanged.
- **Moving stories:**
  - Draft takes drops, and stories can be dragged among Draft, the Backlog and Next sprint.
  - Card menus: Draft has "Move to backlog"; the Backlog has "Move to next sprint" and "Move to draft".
  - Alt+Right moves a Draft story to the Backlog, and Alt+Left moves a Backlog story to Draft. Alt+Left in Draft does nothing.
  - Ctrl+Enter in Draft moves the story to the Backlog. Send sprint still takes only Next sprint, so a Draft story never reaches a sprint directly.
- **Selection and bulk bar:** Draft stories can be selected, ordered Draft, then Backlog, then Next sprint. The bulk bar has a new "Move to draft", and its "Move to backlog" now moves Draft stories as well as Next sprint ones.
- **Saving:** `order.json` has a `draft` section, closing a sprint saves it too, and an older plan without one loads with Draft empty.

I added a test for saving Draft and loading an old plan without it. I also updated the column-colour test, which no longer requires Draft and the Backlog to have different top edges because the spec gives them the same colour, and the F6 test, which now counts Draft as the first column.

`src/planning.rs` isn't tracked by git, so these changes won't show in `git status`. The other modified files listed there were already changed and aren't mine.
